context: Radial dendrogram with hierarchical edge bundling showing software module dependencies: ~120 leaf nodes across 7 top-level modules (core, network, storage, auth, ui, api, testing), 80 cross-module dependency edges rendered on canvas with Bézier bundling at 0.85 tension, hover highlighting, and a tension slider.
first_impression: The bundling keeps the center from becoming a hairball and the 7-color Tol palette cleanly encodes modules, but the sheer density of the leaf ring and 9.5px labels make the static view feel cramped.
what_works: High tension (0.85) bundles the 80 edges into legible arcs rather than spaghetti, and the two-pass canvas render (dim all, highlight hovered) is a strong interaction design that rescues readability at this scale. The Tol colorblind-safe palette stays perceptually distinct across all 7 categories simultaneously.
what_doesnt: With ~120 leaves packed around the ring, the radial labels overlap and become nearly unreadable at the default viewport without hovering — the 9.5px font size is at or below the viable minimum. The key usability mechanism (hover to isolate connections) cannot be assessed from a static screenshot, meaning the chart's actual effectiveness depends entirely on interaction quality that isn't visible here.
